accuracy_findings.claim: System penalties are percentage reductions of a system's outputs, applied after every bonus.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1321 runs Core.Bonus.apply_bonuses over all bonuses (buildings, station, initial, happiness, outside); the penalties are applied afterwards at :1339-1341 as :mul bonuses of -coeff (:1376-1390). Run tmp/help-review/system-penalties-acc-r0-run.exs: base prod=150.0 (100 add + 50 from a :mul lex) is reduced only after the bonus pass.

accuracy_findings.claim: There are three, each shown in the reduced output's tooltip under its own label.
accuracy_findings.evidence: Three apply_penalties calls at stellar_system.ex:1339-1341 (siege, workforce, uprising). Each adds a detail with reason {:misc, :under_siege_penalties|:workforce_penalties|:uprising_penalties} (:1379). ResourceDetail.vue:71-72 renders misc reasons via resource-detail.misc.*; the labels are in game.json:1572-1574 (Besieged / Over-mobilized population / Insufficient stability). Run details: prod misc [workforce_penalties -30.0, uprising_penalties -30.0]. Details.vue attaches resource-detail to fighter_lvl and remove_contact too. Nuance from the run: under siege, the production tooltip also lists the workforce and uprising lines with value -0.0.

accuracy_findings.claim: Besieged: applies when the system is under siege; reduces Production only; size 100 %
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1330 siege_penalty = 1 when state.siege != nil; :1367-1368 uses @limited_penalty_fields = [:sys_production] (:12). Run 'page example + siege': +siege prod 150.0 -> 0.0, credit 80 unchanged, tech 10 unchanged.

accuracy_findings.claim: Over-mobilized population: applies when mobilized workforce is greater than total; reduces the standard list; size 1 − total / mobilized
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1332-1335 workforce_penalty = 1 - workforce/used_workforce when used_workforce > workforce, else 0; :1370-1371 uses @standard_penalty_fields. Run: used=15, workforce=12 -> wp=0.19999999999999996; prod 150 -> 120.0.

accuracy_findings.claim: Insufficient stability: applies when the population status is not Normal; size set by the status (link population-status)
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1341 applies pop_status.penalty; the :1364 clause skips a coeff of 0. PopulationStatus content: normal 0, discontent 0.1, demonstration 0.25, uprising 0.5, general_uprising 0.8 (printed by the run). Run 'normal status only wf': no uprising_penalties detail added.

accuracy_findings.claim: The last two reduce Production, Credit, Technology, Ideology, Defense, Intelligence, Cybersecurity, and the initial XP of the four ship classes.
accuracy_findings.evidence: @standard_penalty_fields stellar_system.ex:18-30 = sys_production, sys_credit, sys_technology, sys_ideology, sys_defense, sys_ci, sys_remove_contact, sys_fighter_lvl, sys_corvette_lvl, sys_frigate_lvl, sys_capital_lvl. Names render as Intelligence/Cybersecurity (data.json:159-161, 82-84). Run: tech 10 -> 8.0 -> 6.0, fighter 5 -> 4.0 -> 3.0. For Cybersecurity the part goes into DynamicValue.change (dynamic-value.ex:24-35), i.e. the rate the UI shows (Details.vue:237).

accuracy_findings.claim: No penalty reduces stability, housing, mobility or S.L.S.D.
accuracy_findings.evidence: sys_happiness, sys_habitation, sys_mobility and sys_radar are in neither list (stellar_system.ex:12, :18-30). Run: happy=20 and mob=30 unchanged through all three penalties.

accuracy_findings.claim: Penalties apply in the order of the table.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1339-1341 pipe order: siege, then workforce, then uprising, which is the table's row order.

accuracy_findings.claim: Each takes its percentage of what the earlier ones left, so they multiply rather than add.
accuracy_findings.evidence: apply_penalties/4 (stellar_system.ex:1376-1390) passes base_state: state, the state received from the previous penalty call, and Core.Bonus.get_input reads :mul input from base_state (bonus.ex:94-ish get_input). Run: 20 % workforce + 25 % Protests gives prod 150 -> 120.0 -> 90.0 (compounding). An additive result would have been 82.5.

accuracy_findings.claim: Each is taken from the output's full total, bonuses from buildings, lexes and agents included.
accuracy_findings.evidence: Penalty base = state after apply_bonuses (stellar_system.ex:1321), which includes building bonuses, player bonuses (lexes/traditions via Player.extract_bonus policy_bonuses player.ex ~1055-1066, pushed with {:update_bonuses, :player, ...}) and the governor's bonuses (push_character :governor, stellar_system.ex:819-826). Run: prod base 150.0 = 100 building add + 50.0 lex :mul; the workforce penalty removed -30.0 = 20 % of 150, not of 100. Nuance: 'agents' here means the system's governor only.

accuracy_findings.claim: An output below zero is not reduced.
accuracy_findings.evidence: bonus.ex:21 returns 0 for a :mul when previous_value.value < 0. Run 'negative credit': credit -40 stays -40 after both penalties (detail parts value 0). Minor nuance: for Cybersecurity the guard checks the accumulator .value, not the displayed rate.

accuracy_findings.claim: Example: 12 of 15 workers (20 %) ...
accuracy_findings.evidence: The 20 % needs used_workforce 15 > workforce 12 (1 - 12/15 = 0.19999999999999996, stellar_system.ex:1332-1335). '12 of 15 workers' reads as 12 mobilized out of 15 population. Run with used=12, workforce=15: wp=0, no workforce penalty, prod 150 -> 112.5 from Protests alone.
accuracy_findings.fix: Say it the right way round, e.g. "15 workforce mobilized with only 12 population (1 − 12/15 = 20 %) and Protests (25 %)".

accuracy_findings.claim: ... and Protests (25 %)
accuracy_findings.evidence: population_status.ex demonstration penalty: 0.25 (run printed demonstration: 0.25); {name:population_status.demonstration} renders 'Protests' in the --text output. Note the 25 % is a content-table value; the page cites no population_status source.

accuracy_findings.claim: production 150 → 120 → 90
accuracy_findings.evidence: Run 'page example': base prod=150.0, +wf prod=120.0, +upr prod=90.0.

accuracy_findings.claim: credit 80 → 64 → 48
accuracy_findings.evidence: Run 'page example': base credit=80, +wf credit=64.0, +upr credit=48.0.

accuracy_findings.claim: also under siege: production 0, credit 48
accuracy_findings.evidence: Run 'page example + siege': +siege prod=0.0, final prod=0.0 credit=48.0.

accuracy_findings.claim: Temporary penalties, such as a Destabilize, are a different thing: they lower stability, not outputs.
accuracy_findings.evidence: collect_happiness_penalties (stellar_system.ex:1892-1899) emits only :add from :direct of -value to :sys_happiness; entries are pushed at :868 (Destabilize = encourage_hate, game.json:409). They never touch the output fields directly.

accuracy_findings.claim: (missing) A temporary stability penalty can still reduce outputs indirectly: if it pushes stability to 0 or below, the population status changes and the Insufficient stability penalty applies.
accuracy_findings.evidence: Happiness penalties feed apply_bonuses (stellar_system.ex:1312, :1321). update_population_status (:1543-1551) then picks the status from the post-bonus happiness (discontent threshold 0, `<=`), and :1341 applies that status's penalty to outputs. As written, 'not outputs' can be read as 'never affects outputs'.
accuracy_findings.fix: Add one clause, e.g. "they lower [[stability]], not outputs directly; if stability drops far enough, the population status changes and Insufficient stability applies."

accuracy_findings.claim: (missing) 'Under siege' also covers a Bombard or Pillage in progress, not only a conquest.
accuracy_findings.evidence: StellarSystem.besiege sets state.siege (stellar_system.ex:281-287) and is called by conquest.ex:88 ({:besiege, :conquest,...}), raid.ex:70 ({:besiege, :raid,...}) and loot.ex:70 ({:besiege, :loot,...}). siege_penalty at :1330 only checks siege != nil, so production is 0 during any of the three.
accuracy_findings.fix: In the Applies-when cell: "a Navarch is conquering, bombarding or pillaging the system" (siege page is planned, plain text).

accuracy_findings.claim: sources: stellar_system.ex:12-30, :1319-1341, :1364-1390, bonus.ex:13-57

clarity_findings.quote: Example: 12 of 15 workers (20 %) and {name:population_status.demonstration} (25 %):
clarity_findings.problem: This caption line sits outside the indented example block (which begins on the next line), so its numbers (12, 15, 20%, 25%) are bare literals in plain prose rather than tokens or contents of an indented example. The numbers rule only exempts computed numbers that are inside a 4-space-indented example block.
clarity_findings.fix: Fold the setup into the indented block itself (e.g. put the whole worked example, including the '12 of 15' and '(20%)/(25%)' framing, inside the indented lines), or rephrase the caption without literal figures: 'Example: a system with more mobilized workforce than it has, and a population in Protests:' and let the indented lines carry all the numbers.

clarity_findings.quote: the outputs listed below | 1 − total / mobilized, see workforce ... the outputs listed below | set by the status, see population-status
clarity_findings.problem: In the table, 'mobilized workforce is greater than total' (Applies when column) and 'the population status is not Normal' (Applies when column) both name the mechanic before any link appears — the [[workforce]] and [[population-status]] links only show up two cells later, in the Size column of the same row. A reader hits the term unlinked first.
clarity_findings.fix: Put the link on the first mention instead: '...the [[workforce|mobilized workforce]] is greater than total' and '...the [[population-status|population status]] is not Normal', and drop (or keep only as a repeat, not the sole link) the later 'see [[...]]' phrasing.

clarity_findings.quote: Example: 12 of 15 workers (20 %) and {name:population_status.demonstration} (25 %):

clarity_findings.quote: No penalty reduces stability, housing, mobility or S.L.S.D.
clarity_findings.problem: S.L.S.D. is an undefined acronym here with no link and no expansion anywhere reachable from this page, even though the detection system it names is covered by the existing, linkable map-legend page. A first-time reader has no way to learn what it stands for.

clarity_findings.quote: Temporary penalties, such as a Destabilize, are a different thing
clarity_findings.problem: 'Destabilize' is named with zero context — no link (no page exists yet) and no gloss of what it is or who performs it. A reader who hasn't met this action elsewhere is left guessing.

clarity_findings.quote: Each is taken from the output's full total, bonuses from buildings, lexes and agents included.

clarity_findings.quote: The last two reduce {name:bonus_pipeline_out.sys_production}, {name:bonus_pipeline_out.sys_credit}, ...
clarity_findings.problem: 'The last two' forces the reader to scroll back and count table rows to figure out it means the workforce and uprising penalties (as opposed to besieged). This is an unnecessary indirection for a one-sentence lookup.
